links.outcome: User accuracy with vs without AI assistance in medication order verification; overreliance assessed
links.effect: AI assistance raised overall accuracy (adjusted OR 1.58; 95% CI 1.16-2.15). Correct AI recommendations raised accuracy to 80.2%, incorrect AI recommendations lowered it to 26.1%.
links.quote: AI assistance was associated with significantly higher overall accuracy (adjusted odds ratio, 1.58; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-2.15).

links.outcome: Automation bias: acceptance of incorrect AI recommendations and accuracy when disagreeing with AI
links.effect: Participants accepted 80.2% of correct and 73.9% of incorrect recommendations; accuracy dropped to 21.7% when users disagreed with the AI.
links.quote: Participants demonstrated high concordance with AI suggestions, accepting 80.2% of correct recommendations and 73.9% of incorrect recommendations.

links.outcome: Clinician accuracy as used with AI in workflow versus unassisted, by experience level
links.effect: AI-assisted accuracy was higher (aOR 1.58); benefit greatest among students, least among PGY2 residents; accuracy depended on AI correctness.
links.quote: Subgroup analysis showed the greatest benefit among students and the least benefit among PGY2 residents.

screen.reason: Randomized simulation trial evaluating the effect of LLM decision support on pharmacist verification accuracy and quantifying automation bias compared to unassisted review.

primary.practice: AI-assisted clinical decision support versus unassisted review
